newsitem.title: BELGIUM: CHOCOLATE MAKER NEUHAUS POSITIVE OUTLOOK.
newsitem.headline: CHOCOLATE MAKER NEUHAUS POSITIVE OUTLOOK.

text.p: Shares in Belgian luxury chocolate maker Neuhaus NV dipped slightly on Wednesday after a meteoric performance on the first day of trading on Tuesday, but dealers shrugged it off saying the company was a good buy.
"It's a nice small cap company which offers a nice yield and growth opportunity and has a sound balance sheet," said trader Benoit Kint at brokerage Petercam.
The share, which jumped 24 percent on the first day of bourse trading, was expected to hold steady at present levels.
"2,150 francs is a sound and fair level, it should remain well orientated and remain positive for medium and long term investors," Kint added.
By 1345 GMT the share was down 0.9 percent at 2,150 francs, with 35,500 shares traded. The initial public offering (IPO) was priced at 1,750 francs.
Controlling shareholder Artal Nederland BV last month sold 450,000 Neuhaus shares in an IPO.
Trader Paul de Lophem at brokerage Mignon, Hanart, Declerck put down the recent price jump to investors looking for new investment opportunities in Belgium.
"There's recently been a lack of IPO's and the market is looking for new possibilities to invest," he said.
De Lophem expected the remaining 40 percent stake, or 350,000 shares, Artal controls in Neuhaus to be sold soon.
But Kint said he expected Artal to hang on for at least the next six months.
Artal and Neuhaus were not available for comments.
Dealers said institutions which found themselves squeezed out of the 15 times oversubscribed IPO were the main buyers, keen to build up their positions.
Kint said investors had not picked up the stock because of takeover rumours but because it was an attractive stock.
"It has a decent growth with an aggressive policy abroad," he added.
Dealers said Neuhaus, famous for its praline chocolates and considered by many as the best praline maker in Belgium, would also benefit in an industry which sees an eight percent yearly growth.
